seo.title: Cloudflare D1 client for {devices}
seo.description: Connect to Cloudflare D1 with an account ID and an API token, move between the account’s databases, and query them in SQLite’s dialect with plan diagrams.

header.title: Cloudflare D1 client
header.lead: Browse the D1 databases in your Cloudflare account and run SQLite queries through Cloudflare’s API.

bands.title: Connect with an API token
text: Enter a D1 database name or UUID, your Cloudflare account ID and an <ui>API Token</ui>, which stays in the <credentials>macOS Keychain</credentials>. Requests use HTTPS, so there is no host, port, TLS setting or SSH tunnel.

Create the token with Account > D1 > Edit permission and copy it when it is shown. It grants access to every D1 database in the account, not just the one you pick. Importing a d1://account-id/database-name URL fills in the account and the database; the token never travels in the URL, so paste it in afterwards.

bands.title: Switch databases and query
text: Switch between the account’s D1 databases without reconnecting; the switcher also creates and drops databases, and open tabs keep their starting database. Queries use <sqlite>SQLite</sqlite>’s dialect, and <explain>EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN</explain> is drawn as a diagram.

Write each statement so it stands on its own: a PRAGMA setting or a temporary table made by one statement is gone by the next, and every statement commits when it runs, with nothing to roll back. When Cloudflare rate-limits a request, the error carries the wait it asked for before a retry.

bands.title: Tables, indexes and triggers
text: The <structure>Structure tab</structure> creates and drops tables, adds and drops columns, and creates and drops indexes, partial indexes with a WHERE condition included. The Triggers tab creates, edits and drops triggers, and tables can be renamed from the sidebar.

A column reorder or a foreign key change means rebuilding the table. TablePro writes that rebuild script and hands it to you to run, because every statement is a separate request and no transaction can hold the rebuild together.

moveData: Export a D1 table or a query result as {exportFormats}. To load a SQL file, run wrangler d1 execute with its --file option, then browse the result here.

faq.question: Does TablePro use D1’s Sessions API?
faq.answer: No. Each statement goes out as its own request, with no session and no bookmark, so nothing carries over from one statement to the next, in one tab or across tabs.

faq.question: Do I need Wrangler installed?
faq.answer: Not to browse, query or edit: TablePro talks to Cloudflare’s API directly. Wrangler is only needed to load a SQL file.
